top_signals.title: Gold Falls as Inflation Fears Revive Fed Interest-Rate Hike Bets
top_signals.summary: Gold fell as renewed strength in energy prices, particularly oil, and the latest US data on manufacturing and services reinforced bets that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates to fight inflation.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: No Slowdown Expected Ahead of Midterms: Top Dealmakers
top_signals.summary: JPMorgan Global Head of M&A Charlie Bouckaert and Weil Partner Michael Aiello discuss global dealmaking trends, AI disruption, and the "war for talent" with Dani Burger and David Carnevali on "Bloomberg Deals." (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: What goes into diesel prices?
top_signals.summary: The price of distillate fuel oil, often sold as diesel, is driven by the price of crude oil, retail margins, distribution costs, taxes, and crack spreads, the indicator we use for refining margins. Tight global supplies of distillate fuel oil and elevated crude oil prices have driven prices higher in recent months.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Commodity repricing impacting inflation expectations and industrial supply chains.

top_signals.title: What the End of Operation Inherent Resolve Means for Iraq and Syria
top_signals.summary:
Operation Inherent Resolve is scheduled to end on Sept. 30, as remaining U.S. troops in northern Iraq complete their withdrawal. The United States formed Combined Joint Task Force – Operation Inherent Resolve in October 2014 to bring together partners to combat the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL), which had seized territory in parts of Iraq and Syria. The end of Operation Inherent Resolve highlights the success of coalition efforts against ISIL but also raises questions about future political stability and security in Iraq and Syria — and whether ISIL could rise again.
